claims.text: A 10–20 nm high-thermal-conductivity interlayer between the substrate and FeMnNiGeSi film will improve heat-transfer rates during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Improved thermal coupling will synchronize thermal extraction with magnetic-domain switching.
Synchronizing thermal extraction and domain switching will increase the isothermal entropy change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Synchronizing thermal extraction and domain switching will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Ti or AlN can serve as the proposed high-thermal-conductivity interlayer.
The interlayer will enhance interfacial thermal connectivity and facilitate rapid heat exchange between the film and substrate.
The interlayer will act as a thermal bridge that reduces thermal lag during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Reduced thermal lag will enable faster heat extraction and re-equilibration.
Improved heat extraction and re-equilibration will minimize kinetic barriers that contribute to hysteresis.
Reduced thermal lag will permit magnetic domains to switch more synchronously with temperature changes.
Interlayer-containing films will show reduced hysteresis, especially at higher cycling frequencies.
Interlayer-containing films will show increased isothermal entropy change, especially at higher cycling frequencies.
Enhanced interfacial heat transfer will correlate with altered magnetic-domain dynamics.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films without an interlayer typically exhibit larger hysteresis and diminished high-frequency magnetocaloric performance because of thermal lag.
The intervention is most relevant near the magnetic transition when cycling frequencies approach limits imposed by film–substrate heat transfer.
